title: Lockport Carnival and Mardi Gras versus Philadelphia's Mummers
summary: They recall Lockport's Carnival on the Saturday before Mardi Gras, then Jones says Philadelphia had no Mardi Gras and the Mummers parade took its place.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Some of your friends told you. In fact I don't even know exactly where it was. It was on the Jefferson Highway, was it?

I never went there either. Other places I went to. But not there. But we're talking about the good old days in Lockport. What day did they have Carnival? It was I think. Could it have been a Tuesday? The Saturday before Mardi Gras. Aha. Yeah that's something I never could figure out. How could Mardi Gras be on a Saturday? Yeah. It was a Saturday before Mardi Gras day. Yeah.

Because most of the people from Lockport would come to New Orleans for Mardi Gras day anyways. Well that makes sense. But it was a while. In fact right after that they started holding it on Fat Tuesday.
Yeah. Did they get many people in from out of town like from Matthews? They had people come from far away. Yeah.
Timedale and all of them. Yeah. It was quite an affair. We had a good time.

Speaking of affairs, I went to Carnival once like that and then we're having Carnival on Sunday. That big day would be Sunday in different towns on the way going down to Grand Isle. But there was nothing on Tuesday on Grand Isle. It was just absolutely a work day. I forget whether the post office was closed or not.
Yeah I found it hard to believe when I moved away from New Orleans. Why didn't people go to work in Philadelphia on Mardi Gras day? I just couldn't understand that.

Yeah. Well, when I was in the Navy, guys would write me from New Orleans and say, Are you coming back for Carnival? It's as though the US Navy would close down for Carnival. Yeah. Okay. Everybody thinks the same way. There was no equivalent in Philadelphia at all.

No. New Year's Day, the Mummers was their Mardi Gras. Held in the dead of winter, snow up to your armpits. And every banjo player for six hundred miles walking down Broad Street freezing to death in these feathered costumes. As many years as I lived in Philadelphia, which was about three, I lived three blocks from where they paraded. I never once saw it. I always watched it on television. It's just too damn cold.
